item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00441","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C09","C03"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 provides a highly concrete drafting template: both proclamations describe a scheduled commercial exhibition, recite a joint resolution authorizing the President to invite the States and foreign countries, state that participation will promote foreign and domestic commerce and foster good will among nations, and conclude with nearly identical invitations to participate. C09 and C03 use the same machinery, but C04 has the closest distinctive language and operative structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 30, 1957 ... authorized the President ... by proclamation or in such other manner as he might deem proper, to invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate","parent_excerpt":"the Congress, by a joint resolution approved July 27, 1956, has authorized the President ... by proclamation or in such other manner as he may deem proper, to invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate","explanation":"Distinctive, closely parallel authorization recital with the same participants and presidential mechanism."},{"child_excerpt":"for the purpose of promoting foreign and domestic commerce and fostering good will among nations","parent_excerpt":"will promote foreign and domestic commerce and will serve as a means of fostering good will among nations","explanation":"Near-verbatim statement of the event's public purposes."},{"child_excerpt":"do hereby invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate in the programs of the Saint Lawrence Seaway Celebration to be held at Chicago, Illinois, in 1959","parent_excerpt":"do hereby invite the States of the Union and foreign countries to participate in the United States World Trade Fair to be held ... in New York, New York, from April 14 to April 27, 1957, inclusive","explanation":"The operative invitation is substantially the same sentence adapted to a different event, place, and date."}]}
